title: Paprika Roasted Chicken Quarters
seoTitle: Paprika Roasted Chicken Quarters | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Budget-friendly leg quarters with smoked paprika rub for ten
subtitle: Budget-friendly leg quarters with smoked paprika rub for ten
description: Chicken leg quarters get a smoky paprika rub and roast on sheet pans until skin crackles and meat pulls cleanly from the bone at 165°F. Simple, filling, and built for hall budgets.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Paprika Roasted Chicken Quarters in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix the rub
steps.instruction: Combine smoked paprika, sweet paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper. Toss quarters with olive oil, then coat evenly with rub.

steps.title: Prep the pans
steps.instruction: Line two sheet pans with parchment. Arrange quarters skin-side up with at least an inch between pieces. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast until fully cooked
steps.instruction: Roast at 400°F for 45–50 minutes until skin is deep golden and thickest part reaches 165°F without touching bone. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Crisp under broiler
steps.instruction: Optional: broil 2–3 minutes for extra crackly skin. Watch closely so paprika does not scorch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Paprika Roasted Chicken Quarters onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Serve family-style
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes, scatter parsley, and pile quarters on platters with lemon wedges for squeezing at the table. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Quarters are done when juices run clear and leg joint moves easily—probe confirms.
Roast quartered potatoes on the same pans during the last 30 minutes.
Hold finished quarters at 165°F max—higher dries dark meat fast.
tonightSpread: Paprika quarters with roasted potatoes and buttered corn.
White rice with pan drippings spooned over for a simple plate.
leftovers: Pull meat for chicken tacos with shredded lettuce and salsa.
Simmer bones into stock for next week's soup base.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Leg quarters are the most forgiving cut on the roster—cheap, hard to overcook, and satisfying after a hard shift. Two pans feed ten without fuss.
mealPrepNotes: Season quarters up to 12 hours ahead for deeper flavor. Use parchment on pans for easier cleanup. Portion one leg quarter per person with extra for big eaters.
